card.hook: Picture a giant C of streetlights curling around the sea, flicking on one pearl at a time. That's Marine Drive at dusk, and the best seat for it is up on a hill.
card.stand_here: Stand on a terrace in Pherozeshah Mehta Gardens (the Hanging Gardens) on Malabar Hill. Face back across the bay towards Marine Drive, and you'll see the whole C-shaped curve with the Arabian Sea beside it and the south Mumbai skyline behind.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to fit the whole curve and the sky. Then try 2x or 5x (depends on your phone) to squeeze the lines of lights and buildings closer together. Only use 0.5x if a railing or trees get in the way, because it makes the far-off curve look small.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines, put the curve of the road along one of the lower lines, keep the horizon level, and once the lights come on try night mode while you rest your elbows on a wall.
card.best_time: Go around sunset, just as the streetlights start to come on and the curve begins to glow. The sun's position along Marine Drive shifts through the year, so arrive early and watch how the light falls.
card.selfie_here: Try the sea wall about midway along the promenade. It's less crowded than the ends, and the Art Deco buildings catch golden light behind you. Use the front camera, hold it a little low, and let the buildings fill the background over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Look for a friendly passer-by on the raised section near the Chowpatty Beach entrance at the north end, and ask them to shoot you so the whole Marine Drive arc fits in the frame.
card.rules_and_safety: The rocks around the tetrapods at the south end can be slippery, so wear shoes with good grip. Officially you're not supposed to climb on the tetrapods, so the sea wall is the safer choice. The Hanging Gardens is a public park, so check opening hours and any entry fee locally before you go.
card.challenge: Take a few frames as the light changes and see if you can catch the exact moment the first streetlights switch on.
card.good_to_know: Marine Drive is a 3-kilometre curved promenade known as the Queen's Necklace, because the streetlights look like a string of pearls from above at night. The road and promenade were built in 1940. Some of the pale art deco blocks behind it, like Kapur Mahal, Zaver Mahal and Keval Mahal, date from 1937 to 1939 and belong to the UNESCO-listed Victorian Gothic and Art Deco Ensembles of Mumbai.

selfie_research.safety: The rocks around the tetrapods can be slippery, so wear shoes with good grip.
selfie_research.notes: Both selfie spots and the passer-by spot come from one guide (mumbaiitinerary.com); the other pages found only general photo advice. The same guide says officially you are not supposed to climb on the tetrapods, so the first selfie spot may not be permitted. The midway spot is described only as a stretch of sea wall, not a named point. No page stated selfie stick or tripod rules; one page recommends using a tripod for night shots, which is advice rather than a rule. Hanging Gardens / Malabar Hill was mentioned as offering a whole-crescent view, but no page gave a selfie or photo position there, so I did not use it.
